deviations_from_adr: Collateral bug fix (not an ADR deviation, but flagged for visibility): src/http/rights-change-requests.ts::listChangeRequests had TWO pre-existing SELECTs referencing `r.name AS role_name`, but choros.role (migration 019) has no `name` column (only `display_name`) — a genuine, unrelated-to-authorization bug that made GET /api/rights/change-requests 500 against a real Postgres whenever any pending item had a role_id (i.e. essentially always in production). Never caught before because the only prior test coverage (src/__tests__/rights-change-requests.test.ts CR-1) uses a stub pool that never validates SQL against a real schema. Fixed both occurrences (r.name -> r.display_name) — required to even prove the new gate's 'authorized sees' positive path against live PG. See docs/tasks/T-0736.adr.md §4.

spec_ref: docs/tasks/T-0726.adr.md §5.2 (three findings this task closes: grant-trail.ts, rights-change-requests.ts, rights-sod.ts), docs/tasks/T-0736.adr.md (this task's mini-ADR)
summary: Three GET rights-family routes passed authentication (withAuth) and tenant-scoping (resolveActorTenant) but never called any of the 7 registered T-0658/T-0662 authority resolvers — confirmed live by the T-0726 judge. Closed all three findings by reusing already-sanctioned resolvers/markers (no new authority path): (1) GET /api/grant-trail -> resolveActorPrivilege(...).isOwnerOrAdmin (admin/owner, same bar as rights-overview.ts's can_manage), 403 FORBIDDEN otherwise. (2) GET /api/rights/change-requests -> assertApproverIsHuman (the SAME registered T-0662 resolver #7 the sibling approve/reject routes on this exact file already carry) — deliberately NOT narrowed to admin/owner, per T-0044 ADR §9 (any distinct active human may be a second approver). (3) GET /api/rights/sod-check -> self-view (subjectId===actorId or omitted) needs no gate (established self-scoped doctrine); subjectId OVERRIDE now requires resolveActorPrivilege(...).isOwnerOrAdmin, 403 BEFORE the target subject's existence is even resolved (no exists/doesn't-exist oracle leak).

resolver_per_route.GET /api/grant-trail: resolveActorPrivilege(pool, tenantId, actor, nowMs).isOwnerOrAdmin — src/db/sandbox-gate-dao.ts (already an ACTIVE_MARKERS Group-2 verified derivative composing loadAdminContext [Group-1 B2] + getGrantsForSubject [Group-1 A]). hasAuthoringDraftGrant is deliberately IGNORED (config-authoring privilege, unrelated to rights-domain visibility).
resolver_per_route.GET /api/rights/change-requests: assertApproverIsHuman(pool, tenantId, actorId) — src/http/rights-change-requests.ts, the registered 7th AUTHORITY_RESOLVERS entry (T-0662 round-2), REUSED verbatim from the sibling approve/reject routes in this same file. NOT admin/owner-narrowed by design (T-0044 ADR §9: any distinct active human is an eligible second approver).
resolver_per_route.GET /api/rights/sod-check: self (subjectId===actorId or omitted): no gate (self-scoped doctrine, mirrors notifications.ts/user-prefs.ts). override (subjectId!==actorId): resolveActorPrivilege(...).isOwnerOrAdmin, same bar as grant-trail.

sod_check_subjectid_policy: subjectId defaults to the authenticated actor (self, ungated). Any override to a DIFFERENT slug requires isOwnerOrAdmin (via resolveActorPrivilege -> loadAdminContext's isGenesisOwner || adminGrants.length>0). An unprivileged override now gets 403 FORBIDDEN with an EMPTY body (no subjectId/conflicts/heldRoles echoed) BEFORE checkSodForSubject ever resolves whether the target subject exists — closes the bare identity-swap hole (T-0726 §5.2, the most dangerous of the three findings) without breaking self-view or a privileged owner's legitimate cross-employee SoD review. Live-PG proof: ci/checks/db/T-0736-rights-sod-check-authz.db.test.ts AC-1..AC-4 (self ok / owner-override sees real target data / unprivileged override 403 no-leak / deactivated-owner-override 403 fail-closed).

who_may_read.grant-trail: admin/owner only (isGenesisOwner || delegable mgmt_object:* admin grants) — full tenant-wide grant/assignment journal is administrative data by construction; no existing precedent in the codebase gives an ordinary member visibility into OTHER employees' grant events.
who_may_read.change-requests: ANY active human (not narrowed to admin/owner) — the pending dual-control queue is a potential-second-approver worklist; T-0044 ADR §9 makes any distinct active human an eligible approver, so narrowing the LIST to admin/owner would have been a product regression (a legitimate non-admin approver could no longer see what's pending).
